summary: The transaction fee is $22.00 per applicable vehicle transaction (sale, lease, fleet, or as-is), effective September 1, 2025, up from $12.50. Dealers self-report and remit as one payment combined with their renewal fee.

sourceLabel: OMVIC — Introducing the New Transaction Fee Reporting Process
summary: Dealers whose registrations renew on or after January 6, 2025 must complete and upload a Transaction Fee Register through the dealer portal. OMVIC states the change followed a pilot project and Auditor General recommendations after finding reporting inconsistencies.

sourceLabel: Auditor General of Ontario — Value-for-Money Audit: OMVIC (2021, full report)
summary: Verified verbatim: of 670 motor vehicle dealers reviewed, 25% (170) under-reported almost 9,000 vehicle transactions in 2019, underpaying about $90,000 in transaction fees. Separately, the number of inspections OMVIC completed was overstated by 3,004 (25%), and OMVIC misreported curbsider-awareness survey data (reported 41% of consumers didn't know what a curbsider is; actual figure was 65%).

sourceLabel: Auditor General of Ontario — OMVIC Follow-Up (2023, Ch. 3.04)
summary: Verified: as of the 2023 follow-up, OMVIC still could not rely on MTO registration data alone to verify dealers' self-reported transaction volumes and was exploring alternatives. The Ministry was also working with OMVIC and FINTRAC on requiring dealers to report large cash transactions, with a policy decision pending as of July 2025 — the MTO/OMVIC data-sharing gap the original audit flagged was still open two years later.

UCDA recommends dealers track fee-applicable transactions daily, or at minimum monthly, rather than reconstructing records at renewal. UCDA has distributed the Transaction Fee Register form to DMS vendors and tells dealers to consult their DMS provider on incorporating it.

UCDA is actively campaigning against OMVIC's fee increases on behalf of dealers, framing the regulator's cost structure as unaffordable — direct evidence that a tool framed as "comply with OMVIC better" will face dealer resistance.
DealerPull markets an OMVIC-compliant garage register as a DMS feature, confirming register/recordkeeping compliance is already treated as a commercial software wedge, not just a manual process.
